# Model and source

Cliramitug (development codes NI006 and ALXN2220) is a human IgG1 antibody that
binds a cryptic epitope exposed only in transthyretin amyloid (ATTR) fibrils and
triggers their removal by phagocytic immune cells. Michalon et al. built a
translational PK/PD model to choose the starting dose, dose range and treatment
duration of the first-in-human phase Ib study NI006-101. The paper contributes
two models:

* `Michalon_2025_cliramitug_rat` -- the rat two-compartment population PK model
  (Table 1) whose estimates were allometrically scaled to human.
* `Michalon_2025_cliramitug_human_qsp` -- the human mechanistic PK/PD (QSP)
  model of cardiac ATTR depletion and left ventricular wall thickness (LVWT).

```{r model-meta}
rat <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Michalon_2025_cliramitug_rat"))
hum <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Michalon_2025_cliramitug_human_qsp"))
```

* Citation: `r hum$reference`
* Rat model: `r rat$description`
* Human model: `r hum$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/cpt.3455> (open access, PMC11652821)

# Population

**Rat.** 36 rats (6 male and 6 female per dose group) received cliramitug IV
as a single 3 or 30 mg/kg dose or as three weekly 300 mg/kg doses; serum was
sampled from 5 minutes to 28 days after dosing (Methods, Figure 1). The model
was fit with SAEM in Monolix.

**Human.** The human model is a forward projection for a typical 70 kg patient
with ATTR cardiomyopathy and a baseline LVWT of 16.6 mm; no patient data were
used to fit it. The disease-progression layer was fitted to published LVWT
values from untreated ATTR-CM patients aged 30 to 76 years and from the
patisiran APOLLO trial. Simulated regimens were 0.3, 1, 3, 10, 30 and 60 mg/kg
every 4 weeks as 2-hour infusions, the doses later studied in NI006-101.

```{r population}
str(rat$population)
str(hum$population)
```

# Source trace

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| Rat `lcl`, `lvc`, `lvp`, `lq` | 0.00245 L/day, 0.0144 L, 0.0189 L, 0.0178 L/day | Table 1, rat column |
| Rat `etalcl`, `etalvc`, `etalvp`, `etalq` | 21%, 10%, 15%, 18% CV | Table 1, brackets; omega^2 = log(1 + CV^2) |
| Rat `propSd` | 0 (fixed) | Not reported |
| Rat ODEs | 2-compartment, IV | Data S1 'Rat PK' Mlxtran |
| Human `lcl`, `lvc`, `lvp`, `lq` | 0.146 L/day, 3.37 L, 4.42 L, 0.676 L/day | Table S1; Table 1 human column |
| `bc_heart` | 0.102 | Table S1 (Shah 2013) |
| `v_heart` | 0.0488 L | Table S1 (Shah 2012) |
| `q_heart` | 0.372 L/day | Table S1 (Shah 2012) |
| `kd` | 2.5 nM | Table S1 (SPR); Results |
| `lkelmax` | 0.066 1/day | Table S1; Results, Figure 2a |
| `lkin` (kgrowth) | 0.43 mm/year | Table S1, Table S2; Results |
| `lkout` (kel) | 0.053 1/year | Table S1, Table S2; Results |
| `lvwt_healthy` | 8.5 mm | Table S2 |
| `lvwt0` | 16.6 mm | Methods 'PK/PD model for predictions'; Results |
| `attr0` | 1.36 g | Table S1; Methods (1% of 136 g) |
| `mw_ab`, `mw_ttr` | 150000, 13750 g/mol | Data S1 'Human PK/PD simulations' |
| `g_per_mm = attr0 / (lvwt0 - lvwt_healthy)` | 0.168 g/mm | Methods LVWT equation; Table S1 'k' |
| Micro-constants `k1h = bc_heart * q_heart / vc`, `kh1 = q_heart / v_heart` | n/a | Data S1 |
| Quasi-equilibrium free antibody in heart | n/a | Data S1 `C_FreeNIh` |
| `d/dt(central)`, `d/dt(peripheral1)`, `d/dt(heart_isf)`, `d/dt(total_target)` | n/a | Data S1 `ddt_FreeNIc`, `ddt_FreeNIp`, `ddt_TotNIh`, `ddt_TotTTRh` |
| `lvwt = total_target / g_per_mm + lvwt_healthy` | n/a | Data S1 `TTRthickness`; Methods equation |

# Rat PK (Figure 1 and Table 1)

```{r rat-sim}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20251)
bw_rat <- 0.3 # kg; the rat reference weight used for allometric scaling
rat_groups <- tibble::tribble(
  ~group, ~dose_mgkg, ~n_dose, ~horizon,
  "3 mg/kg single", 3, 1, 28,
  "30 mg/kg single", 30, 1, 28,
  "300 mg/kg weekly x3", 300, 3, 42
)
make_rat <- function(g, id_offset) {
  ids <- id_offset + seq_len(12)
  dose <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = ids, time = 7 * (seq_len(g$n_dose) - 1)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(amt = g$dose_mgkg * bw_rat, evid = 1L)
  obs <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = ids, time = c(5 / 1440, seq(0.25, g$horizon, by = 0.25))) |>
    dplyr::mutate(amt = NA_real_, evid = 0L)
  dplyr::bind_rows(dose, obs) |>
    dplyr::mutate(cmt = "central", group = g$group) |>
    dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))
}
ev_rat <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(rat_groups)), function(i) {
  make_rat(rat_groups[i, ], id_offset = 12L * (i - 1L))
}))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(ev_rat[, c("id", "time", "evid")])))
sim_rat <- rxode2::rxSolve(rat, events = ev_rat, keep = "group", returnType = "data.frame")
```

```{r rat-fig1}
ggplot(sim_rat, aes(time, Cc, group = id, colour = group)) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.6) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Time (day)", y = "Serum cliramitug (ug/mL)", colour = NULL,
    caption = "Replicates Figure 1 of Michalon 2025 (12 simulated rats per group)."
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

The paper reports no rat NCA; PKNCA summarises the simulated single-dose groups
for reference and confirms dose proportionality.

```{r rat-pknca}
conc_rat <- sim_rat |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc), group != "300 mg/kg weekly x3") |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, group)
conc_rat <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  conc_rat,
  conc_rat |> dplyr::distinct(id, group) |> dplyr::mutate(time = 0, Cc = 0)
) |>
  dplyr::distinct(id, group, time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, group, time)
dose_rat <- ev_rat |>
  dplyr::filter(evid == 1, group != "300 mg/kg weekly x3") |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, amt, group)
nca_rat <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_rat, Cc ~ time | group + id),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_rat, amt ~ time | group + id, route = "intravascular"),
  intervals = data.frame(start = 0, end = 28, cmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE)
))
rat_summary <- as.data.frame(nca_rat) |>
  dplyr::group_by(group, PPTESTCD) |>
  dplyr::summarise(median = median(PPORRES), .groups = "drop") |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = median)
rat_summary |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Group" = group,
    "Cmax (ug/mL)" = cmax,
    "AUC0-28 (ug*day/mL)" = auclast
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Median simulated rat NCA (single-dose groups).")
# Linear PK: AUC per mg/kg agrees between 3 and 30 mg/kg (between-animal
# variability moves the two group medians by a few percent at most).
auc_per_dose <- rat_summary$auclast / c(3, 30)
stopifnot(abs(auc_per_dose[2] / auc_per_dose[1] - 1) < 0.15)
```

## Allometric scaling to human

The human PK parameters in Table 1 come from the rat values with exponents 1
(V1, V2), 0.75 (Cl) and 2/3 (Q), using 0.3 kg for the rat and 70 kg for human.
The check below recomputes them from the packaged rat model and compares them
with the packaged human model.

```{r allometry}
rat_th <- exp(rat$theta[c("lcl", "lvc", "lvp", "lq")])
hum_th <- exp(hum$theta[c("lcl", "lvc", "lvp", "lq")])
scaled <- rat_th * (70 / 0.3)^c(0.75, 1, 1, 2 / 3)
allo <- data.frame(
  parameter = c("Cl (L/day)", "V1 (L)", "V2 (L)", "Q (L/day)"),
  rat = unname(rat_th), scaled = unname(scaled), packaged_human = unname(hum_th)
)
knitr::kable(allo, digits = 4)
# Table 1 prints three significant figures, so allow rounding error only.
stopifnot(all(abs(allo$scaled / allo$packaged_human - 1) < 0.01))
```

# Human QSP model

The human simulations are population-typical predictions with no variability.
One "month" in the paper's Figures 4 to 6 is four weeks: doses fall on the
integer month ticks of Figure 4a, and 12 doses span the 12-month window.

```{r human-events}
days_per_month <- 28
dose_levels <- c(0, 0.3, 1, 3, 10, 30, 60)
dose_label <- function(d) ifelse(d == 0, "Placebo", paste(d, "mg/kg"))
make_human <- function(horizon_months = 26) {
  horizon <- horizon_months * days_per_month
  dose <- tidyr::expand_grid(
    dose_mgkg = dose_levels[dose_levels > 0],
    time = seq(0, horizon - days_per_month, by = days_per_month)
  ) |>
    dplyr::mutate(amt = dose_mgkg * 70, dur = 2 / 24, evid = 1L)
  obs <- tidyr::expand_grid(dose_mgkg = dose_levels, time = seq(0, horizon, by = 0.25)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(amt = NA_real_, dur = NA_real_, evid = 0L)
  dplyr::bind_rows(dose, obs) |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      id = match(dose_mgkg, dose_levels),
      treatment = factor(dose_label(dose_mgkg), levels = dose_label(dose_levels)),
      cmt = "central"
    ) |>
    dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))
}
ev_hum <- make_human()
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(ev_hum[, c("id", "time", "evid")])))

solve_human <- function(params = NULL) {
  rxode2::rxSolve(hum, events = ev_hum, params = params, keep = c("treatment", "dose_mgkg"), returnType = "data.frame") |>
    dplyr::mutate(month = time / days_per_month)
}
sim_base <- solve_human()
```

```

  dplyr::filter(month <= 12) |>

  geom_line() +

sim_base |>
  dplyr::filter(month <= 12) |>
  ggplot(aes(month, lvwt, colour = treatment)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 12, linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 12, 2)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (months)", y = "Cardiac amyloid surrogate (LVWT, mm)", colour = NULL,
    caption = "Replicates Figure 4c of Michalon 2025; dashed line = 12 mm clinical-effect threshold."
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

The paper quotes, for the typical patient: a Cmax of 8.4 ug/mL at 0.3 mg/kg
with ATTR occupancy below 0.1% after the fourth dose, and 22% occupancy after
the fourth monthly 60 mg/kg dose (Results, sensitivity section; Figure 4b).

```{r figure-4-checks}
at_month <- function(sim, m) dplyr::filter(sim, abs(time - m * days_per_month) < 1e-8)
occ4 <- at_month(sim_base, 4)
cmax_4th <- sim_base |>
  dplyr::filter(dose_mgkg == 0.3, time >= 3 * days_per_month, time < 4 * days_per_month) |>
  dplyr::pull(Cc) |>
  max()
cmax_4mo <- sim_base |>
  dplyr::filter(dose_mgkg == 0.3, time <= 4 * days_per_month + 1) |>
  dplyr::pull(Cc) |>
  max()
data.frame(
  quantity = c(
    "Cmax 0.3 mg/kg, 4th dosing interval (ug/mL)",
    "Cmax 0.3 mg/kg, first 4 months incl. the dose at month 4 (ug/mL)",
    "Occupancy 0.3 mg/kg at month 4 (%)",
    "Occupancy 60 mg/kg at month 4 (%)"
  ),
  simulated = c(cmax_4th, cmax_4mo, occ4$occupancy[occ4$dose_mgkg == 0.3], occ4$occupancy[occ4$dose_mgkg == 60]),
  published = c(8.4, 8.4, 0.1, 22)
) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)
stopifnot(
  abs(cmax_4th / 8.4 - 1) < 0.05,
  occ4$occupancy[occ4$dose_mgkg == 0.3] < 0.1,
  abs(occ4$occupancy[occ4$dose_mgkg == 60] - 22) < 1
)
```

## Figure 5: time to clinical effect and sensitivity analyses

Time to clinical effect is the first time LVWT falls below 12 mm. The
sensitivity cases raise the baseline cardiac ATTR load 5- and 10-fold (6.8 and
13.6 g) at the same 16.6 mm starting LVWT, or use the 5.6-fold faster
xenograft elimination rate (kelmax = 0.37/day).

```{r figure-5}
time_to_effect <- function(sim) {
  sim |>
    dplyr::filter(dose_mgkg > 0) |>
    dplyr::group_by(dose_mgkg) |>
    dplyr::summarise(tte = month[which(lvwt < 12)[1]], .groups = "drop")
}
tte <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  time_to_effect(sim_base) |> dplyr::mutate(scenario = "Base case"),
  time_to_effect(solve_human(c(attr0 = 6.8))) |> dplyr::mutate(scenario = "ATTR load 5x"),
  time_to_effect(solve_human(c(attr0 = 13.6))) |> dplyr::mutate(scenario = "ATTR load 10x"),
  time_to_effect(solve_human(c(lkelmax = log(0.37)))) |> dplyr::mutate(scenario = "kelmax 0.37/day")
)
# Values read from Figure 5 by the maintainers; NA = longer than 26 months.
published_tte <- tibble::tribble(
  ~scenario, ~dose_mgkg, ~tte_pub,
  "Base case", 3, 17.8, "Base case", 10, 10.0, "Base case", 30, 6.0, "Base case", 60, 4.4,
  "ATTR load 5x", 10, 21.8, "ATTR load 5x", 30, 12.7, "ATTR load 5x", 60, 9.2,
  "ATTR load 10x", 30, 17.8, "ATTR load 10x", 60, 12.7,
  "kelmax 0.37/day", 0.3, 23.6, "kelmax 0.37/day", 1, 13.1, "kelmax 0.37/day", 3, 7.8,
  "kelmax 0.37/day", 10, 4.5, "kelmax 0.37/day", 30, 2.7, "kelmax 0.37/day", 60, 2.0
)
tte_cmp <- dplyr::full_join(tte, published_tte, by = c("scenario", "dose_mgkg"))

ggplot(dplyr::filter(tte_cmp, !is.na(tte) | !is.na(tte_pub)), aes(dose_mgkg, tte, colour = scenario)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  geom_point(aes(y = tte_pub), shape = 4, size = 3) +
  scale_x_log10(breaks = c(0.3, 1, 3, 10, 30, 60)) +
  labs(
    x = "Dose (mg/kg every 4 weeks)", y = "Time to clinical effect (months)", colour = NULL,
    caption = "Replicates Figure 5 of Michalon 2025; lines = packaged model, crosses = published."
  ) +
  theme_bw()

tte_cmp |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(tte) | !is.na(tte_pub)) |>
  dplyr::arrange(scenario, dose_mgkg) |>
  dplyr::relocate(scenario) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Scenario" = scenario, "Dose (mg/kg)" = dose_mgkg,
    "Simulated (months)" = tte, "Figure 5 (months)" = tte_pub
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)

# Deterministic model, so the only slack needed is the reading precision of
# the figure (about 0.3 month); a missing point on either side must agree.
stopifnot(
  identical(is.na(tte_cmp$tte), is.na(tte_cmp$tte_pub)),
  all(abs(tte_cmp$tte - tte_cmp$tte_pub) < 0.5, na.rm = TRUE)
)
occ4_10x <- at_month(solve_human(c(attr0 = 13.6)), 4)
stopifnot(abs(occ4_10x$occupancy[occ4_10x$dose_mgkg == 60] - 1.8) < 0.2) # Results: 22% -> 1.8%
```

## Figure 6: predicted amyloid change against cumulative exposure

Figure 6 overlays the observed phase Ib imaging changes on the model-predicted
relative change in cardiac amyloid (here the change in ATTR mass, equal to the
change in excess LVWT) against the predicted cumulative AUC at 4 and 12 months.
PKNCA computes the AUCs from the typical-value serum profiles.

```{r figure-6-pknca}
conc_hum <- sim_base |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc), dose_mgkg > 0, time <= 12 * days_per_month) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, treatment)
dose_hum <- ev_hum |>
  dplyr::filter(evid == 1, time <= 12 * days_per_month) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, amt, treatment)
intervals_hum <- data.frame(
  start = c(0, 0, 3 * days_per_month),
  end = c(4 * days_per_month, 12 * days_per_month, 4 * days_per_month),
  auclast = c(TRUE, TRUE, FALSE),
  cmax = c(FALSE, FALSE, TRUE)
)
nca_hum <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_hum, Cc ~ time | treatment + id),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_hum, amt ~ time | treatment + id, route = "intravascular"),
  intervals = intervals_hum
))
sim_nca <- as.data.frame(nca_hum) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    window = dplyr::case_when(
      PPTESTCD == "cmax" ~ "4th dosing interval",
      end == 4 * days_per_month ~ "0-4 months",
      TRUE ~ "0-12 months"
    ),
    # ug*day/mL -> mg*day/mL, the unit of Figure 6
    PPORRES = ifelse(PPTESTCD == "auclast", PPORRES / 1000, PPORRES),
    treatment = as.character(treatment)
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(treatment, window, PPTESTCD, PPORRES)

# AUCs read from the Figure 6 x-axis by the maintainers (log scale, about
# +/-10%); Cmax 8.4 ug/mL from the Results text.
published_nca <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment, ~window, ~auclast, ~cmax,
  "0.3 mg/kg", "0-4 months", 0.33, NA,
  "1 mg/kg", "0-4 months", 1.1, NA,
  "3 mg/kg", "0-4 months", 3.4, NA,
  "10 mg/kg", "0-4 months", 11.5, NA,
  "30 mg/kg", "0-4 months", 33, NA,
  "60 mg/kg", "0-4 months", 68, NA,
  "0.3 mg/kg", "0-12 months", 1.3, NA,
  "1 mg/kg", "0-12 months", 4.2, NA,
  "3 mg/kg", "0-12 months", 12.5, NA,
  "10 mg/kg", "0-12 months", 41, NA,
  "30 mg/kg", "0-12 months", 125, NA,
  "60 mg/kg", "0-12 months", 270, NA,
  "0.3 mg/kg", "4th dosing interval", NA, 8.4
)
cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = sim_nca,
  reference = published_nca,
  by = c("treatment", "window"),
  units = c(auclast = "mg*day/mL", cmax = "ug/mL"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "Simulated vs. published exposure. * differs from reference by >20%.")
stopifnot(!any(grepl("*", cmp[["% diff"]], fixed = TRUE)))
```

```{r figure-6}
change <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  at_month(sim_base, 4) |> dplyr::mutate(window = "0-4 months"),
  at_month(sim_base, 12) |> dplyr::mutate(window = "0-12 months")
) |>
  dplyr::filter(dose_mgkg > 0) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    pct_change = 100 * (total_target / hum$theta[["attr0"]] - 1),
    treatment = as.character(treatment)
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(treatment, dose_mgkg, window, pct_change) |>
  dplyr::left_join(
    sim_nca |> dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast") |> dplyr::select(treatment, window, auc = PPORRES),
    by = c("treatment", "window")
  )
# Model-predicted points read from Figure 6 by the maintainers.
published_change <- tibble::tribble(
  ~dose_mgkg, ~window, ~pct_pub,
  0.3, "0-4 months", 0, 1, "0-4 months", -1, 3, "0-4 months", -3,
  10, "0-4 months", -10, 30, "0-4 months", -27, 60, "0-4 months", -49,
  0.3, "0-12 months", -3, 1, "0-12 months", -10, 3, "0-12 months", -29,
  10, "0-12 months", -74, 30, "0-12 months", -100, 60, "0-12 months", -100
)
change <- dplyr::left_join(change, published_change, by = c("dose_mgkg", "window"))

ggplot(change, aes(auc, pct_change)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(aes(colour = treatment), size = 3) +
  geom_point(aes(y = pct_pub), shape = 4, size = 3) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  facet_wrap(~ factor(window, levels = c("0-4 months", "0-12 months"))) +
  labs(
    x = "Total cliramitug AUC (mg*day/mL)", y = "Relative change from baseline\nin cardiac amyloid (%)",
    colour = NULL, caption = "Replicates the model predictions of Figure 6 of Michalon 2025; crosses = published."
  ) +
  theme_bw()

stopifnot(all(abs(change$pct_change - change$pct_pub) < 3))
```

## Disease progression (Figure S1)

Without treatment the excess LVWT sits at the steady state of the turnover
model, kgrowth / kel = 0.43 / 0.053 = 8.1 mm above the 8.5 mm healthy value,
which is the 16.6 mm starting LVWT; the placebo arm in Figure 4c is flat. The
spontaneous half-life of excess LVWT is log(2) / 0.053 = 13 years (Results).
Patisiran was modelled as an 80% reduction of kgrowth; the right panel of
Figure S1 follows a patient from age 60 under that reduction.

```{r figure-s1}
stopifnot(all(abs(sim_base$lvwt[sim_base$dose_mgkg == 0] - 16.6) < 0.01))
stopifnot(abs(log(2) / 0.053 - 13) < 0.1)

ev_pat <- data.frame(id = 1L, time = seq(0, 17 * 365.25, by = 30), evid = 0L, cmt = "central")
sim_pat <- rxode2::rxSolve(hum, events = ev_pat, params = c(lkin = log(0.43 * 0.2)), returnType = "data.frame") |>
  dplyr::mutate(age = 60 + time / 365.25)
ggplot(sim_pat, aes(age, lvwt)) +
  geom_line(colour = "red") +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(60, 76), ylim = c(0, 20)) +
  labs(
    x = "Age (years)", y = "LVWT (mm)",
    caption = "Replicates the patisiran panel (right) of Figure S1 of Michalon 2025."
  ) +
  theme_bw()
lvwt_at <- function(age) approx(sim_pat$age, sim_pat$lvwt, xout = age)$y
# Figure S1 right panel, read by the maintainers: about 16.1 mm at 61.5 years
# (18 months of patisiran) and 12.9 mm at 76 years.
stopifnot(abs(lvwt_at(61.5) - 16.1) < 0.3, abs(lvwt_at(76) - 12.9) < 0.3)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Drug name.** The paper uses the development codes NI006 and ALXN2220. The
  files use the INN cliramitug, under which the long-term phase Ib follow-up
  was published (Nature Medicine 2026); the maintainers verified the
  assignment on 2026-11-01.
- **Disease-progression equation.** The Methods print
  dLVWT/dt = kgrowth - kel * LVWT on total LVWT, whose steady state
  (0.43 / 0.053 = 8.1 mm) would lie below the healthy 8.5 mm. The deposited
  Mlxtran code (Data S1) applies the turnover to the excess above 8.5 mm (the
  ATTR mass), whose steady state is 16.6 mm -- the paper's baseline LVWT and
  the asymptote of Figure S1. The packaged model follows the code.
- **ATTR state in grams.** The code tracks ATTR in nmol of TTR monomer; the
  package tracks the same quantity as mass in grams (`total_target`) and
  converts to nM for binding with the 13750 g/mol monomer weight. The two are
  identical because every ATTR term is linear in the ATTR amount. Antibody
  amounts are in mg and are converted to nM with 150000 g/mol, again as in
  the code.
- **LVWT per ATTR mass.** Table S1 prints the slope as
  (16.6 - 8.5) / (136 * 0.01) = 6 mm/g; the model uses the unrounded
  expression (5.96 mm/g, as `attr0 / (lvwt0 - lvwt_healthy)` in g/mm). The ATTR
  load sensitivity cases are reproduced by raising `attr0` at a fixed 16.6 mm
  starting LVWT, which scales the ATTR formation rate with it, as
  `TTRkprod_mass = TTRkprod * g_per_mm` does in the code.
- **Year length.** kgrowth and kel are reported per year and converted with
  365.25 days per year; the paper does not state its conversion.
- **Month length.** The figures use four-week months (see the human
  simulation section); reproducing Figures 4 to 6 to within reading precision
  confirms it.
- **Cmax at 0.3 mg/kg.** The simulated Cmax in the fourth dosing interval is
  8.2 ug/mL; the 8.4 ug/mL quoted by the paper is reached by the dose given at
  month 4. Both are within 3%.
- **Occupancy at 60 mg/kg after the fourth dose.** The Results quote both 30%
  (safe-starting-dose section) and 22% (sensitivity section). Figure 4b and the
  packaged model give 22% at month 4; the 30% figure is reached during the
  fifth dosing interval.
- **Fixed versus estimated.** In the human model, the literature and physical
  constants (heart biodistribution coefficient, volume and exchange clearance,
  KD, healthy and baseline LVWT, ATTR mass, molecular weights) are wrapped in
  `fixed()`. The PK parameters (scaled from the rat fit), kelmax (fitted to the
  ex vivo assay) and kgrowth and kel (fitted to LVWT data) were estimated
  within the paper and are left unwrapped, although the human model itself was
  never fitted.
- **No variability in the human model.** The Mlxtran code accepts
  log-normal standard deviations for Cl, V1, V2 and Q, but the paper states
  that all human simulations were population-typical and reports no human
  values; none are attached. The rat between-animal variability is not carried
  to human.
- **Rat model.** The between-animal variability in Table 1 is given as %CV and
  is converted with omega^2 = log(1 + CV^2). The residual-error model is not
  reported and is held at zero. The rat strain and body weights are not
  reported; the vignette doses a 0.3 kg rat, the reference weight used for
  scaling, and gives the doses as IV boluses because the infusion duration is
  not reported.
- **Sub-models not packaged.** The fits that produced kelmax -- the ex vivo
  tissue amyloid depletion assay model and the mouse fibril-xenograft model
  (Data S1) -- are not packaged. Their nuisance parameters (initial amyloid
  area and area-to-concentration factor; mouse V1, Cl, initial fibril
  concentration and spontaneous elimination rate) are not reported; only
  their kelmax estimates (0.066 and 0.37 per day) are, and both are used here.
- **Updated phase III model.** The Discussion notes that the parameters were
  later updated with the phase Ib results for phase III design; those values
  are not published in this paper.
- **Errata.** No correction notice was found for this article as of
  2026-11-01.
